note: The awkward case. Narrative history has weak prerequisite structure — much of the order is chronology, not dependency. Kept as a fixture to watch whether the pipeline produces a corridor with no junctions.

goal.statement: Explain why the Bastille was stormed in July 1789, in terms of what had happened in the preceding months.
goal.audience: an adult who remembers no school history

capstone.prompt: A friend says the Revolution happened because the people were hungry. What is right about that, and what does it leave out?
rubric: does not reduce it to bread alone

assumed: general familiarity with European history and historical analysis techniques

kcs.label: Economic conditions in France before the French Revolution
misconceptions: The economy was not a factor in the revolution
The economy was stable before the revolution
Economic hardship only affected the poor

check.stem: How did economic conditions in France contribute to the onset of the French Revolution?
options: Economic stability delayed the onset of the revolution
Economic conditions only affected elites
Widespread economic hardship fueled unrest against the monarchy.
The economy had no impact on the revolution
distractorSource: The economy was stable before the revolution
Economic hardship only affected the poor
The economy was not a factor in the revolution

kcs.label: Social inequality in pre-revolutionary France
misconceptions: The middle class had equal opportunities

check.stem: What role did social inequality play in the lead-up to the French Revolution?
options: Social inequality was minimal during this period
The middle class had significant influence
Peasants were politically empowered
It created resentment among the lower classes who lacked political power.
distractorSource: The middle class had equal opportunities

kcs.label: Political tensions in France prior to the Bastille storming

check.stem: What were the political tensions in France before the storming of the Bastille?
options: Growing dissatisfaction with the monarchy and lack of representation.
The monarchy was widely supported
Political stability was maintained
There were no political divisions at the time

kcs.label: Impact of the Estates-General meeting in 1789
misconceptions: It increased support for the monarchy

check.stem: What was the impact of the Estates-General meeting in 1789?
options: It successfully addressed social issues
It highlighted and deepened the political crisis by failing to address grievances.
The meeting bolstered support for the monarchy
It had no significant impact historically
distractorSource: It increased support for the monarchy

kcs.label: Formation of the National Assembly
misconceptions: The National Assembly was formed with royal support
It was formed after the Bastille storming

check.stem: Why was the formation of the National Assembly an important step towards the revolution?
options: The National Assembly had royal backing
It consisted solely of wealthy individuals
It marked a direct challenge to the king's authority.
It was established after the Bastille was stormed
distractorSource: The National Assembly was formed with royal support
It was formed after the Bastille storming

kcs.label: Factors leading to the storming of the Bastille
misconceptions: It occurred spontaneously without any buildup

check.stem: Why was the storming of the Bastille a consequential event?
options: The storming was merely a symbolic act with no deeper meaning
It had no significance militarily
It happened spontaneously without any prior issues
It was a symbolic act of rebellion and a response to political and economic tensions.
distractorSource: It occurred spontaneously without any buildup
